question.problem:
The duration (in seconds) of the songs recorded by a music company is normally distributed with a mean of $230\,\text{s}$ and a standard deviation of $40\,\text{s}.$ What is the probability that a randomly selected song recorded by this company has a duration less than or equal to $180\,\text{s}?$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.3\,$ | $\,0.0901\,$ | $\,0.0885\,$ | $\,0.0869\,$ |
| $\,-1.2\,$ | $\,0.1075\,$ | $\,0.1056\,$ | $\,0.1038\,$ |
| $\,-1.1\,$ | $\,0.1271\,$ | $\,0.1251\,$ | $\,0.1230\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the duration (in seconds) of the selected song. Then we have $X∼N(230,{40}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(X<180).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<180) & =P(Z\le \frac{180-230}{40}) \\  & =P(Z\le -1.25) \\  & =Φ(-1.25)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(-1.25)=0.1056≈0.11.
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected song recorded by this company has a duration less than or equal to $180\,\text{s}$ is approximately $0.11.$
